methodology: static-only (read-only extraction from password-protected quarantine zip into 0700 tmpfs; objdump i386 + capstone disasm; strings; ssdeep; single-byte XOR + base64 IOC brute; YARA. NO sample was executed.)

findings.description: Sample 17 (pid 23476, f-response-lm-): Volatility malfind 8192-byte injected RWX page, Variant A of the SRL-2015 VB6 self-injecting loader. 8-byte little-endian length header (0x08) then E9 JMP at offset 8 (E9 F7 07 00 00 = jmp 0x804) into the entry routine, which uses a classic EBP stack frame (55 8B EC / 83 EC 34). Entry takes a struct of pre-resolved kernel32 pointers ([+0x08]=VirtualAlloc, [+0x0C]=VirtualFree), computes a buffer size from header byte[hdr+4] (idiv 9, idiv 5, ((0x300<<cl)+0x736)<<4), VirtualAlloc(NULL,size,MEM_COMMIT,PAGE_READWRITE), calls the LZMA-range-decoder worker at offset 0x0D, then VirtualFree(MEM_RELEASE). msvbvm60 (VB6 runtime) referenced; APIs resolved by plaintext name (OpenProcess/VirtualProtect/GetModuleHandleA), not API hashing.

evidence.network_ioc: none (256-key XOR + base64 brute => 0 readable network indicators)

findings.description: Sample 18 (pid 26340, f-response-lm-): Variant A of the SRL-2015 VB6 self-injecting loader, byte-near-identical (99.1%) to sample 17 and ssdeep 94. Same 8-byte length header + E9 F7 07 00 00 (jmp 0x804) entry stub, EBP stack frame, identical in-memory VirtualAlloc/LZMA-decode/VirtualFree unpack chain. Differences vs 17 are scattered runtime-patched data (handles/addresses/cookies) in the post-code memory-manager region (>=0x900), NOT a configuration block. Same plaintext-name API resolution and OpenProcess/VirtualProtect injection-capability import set.

Sample 19 (pid 145896, f-response-ent): Variant B of the SRL-2015 VB6 self-injecting loader. Same 8-byte length header but E9 60 08 00 00 (jmp 0x86D) entry stub. Entry routine uses an ESP-relative frame (83 EC 30 sub esp,0x30 ; 8B 44 24 34 mov eax,[esp+0x34]) and executes the IDENTICAL size/unpack algorithm as Variant A (read [arg+0x4/+0x8/+0xC], SHL by cl, mov eax,0x300; shl; add 0x736) -> the same source recompiled with different register allocation/optimization. LZMA-range-decoder worker at offset 0x0D. msvbvm60/VB6 origin; plaintext-name API resolution; OpenProcess/VirtualProtect injection capability.

Sample 20 (pid 151132, femc.exe): Variant B of the SRL-2015 VB6 self-injecting loader, masquerading as femc. Byte-near-identical (98.7-98.8%) to samples 19 and 21, ssdeep 91-96. Same 8-byte length header + E9 60 08 00 00 (jmp 0x86D) ESP-frame entry stub and identical in-memory VirtualAlloc/LZMA-decode/VirtualFree unpack chain. femc.exe process masquerade is the only host-context link; no femc/f-response/nfury strings exist inside the payload bytes. Same plaintext-name API resolution and OpenProcess/VirtualProtect injection imports.

Sample 21 (pid 328, f-response-ent on win7-64 nfury): Variant B of the SRL-2015 VB6 self-injecting loader running as a 32-bit (WOW64) injected page on a 64-bit Win7 host (NOT native x64). Byte-near-identical (99.8%) to sample 19 and ssdeep 97 -> highest intra-cluster similarity. Same 8-byte length header + E9 60 08 00 00 (jmp 0x86D) ESP-frame entry stub and identical VirtualAlloc/LZMA-decode/VirtualFree unpack chain. Demonstrates the same loader was deployed across both the win2008R2 controllers and the win7-64 nfury host. Same plaintext-name API resolution and OpenProcess/VirtualProtect injection imports.

Cluster A = {17 (pid23476, 42f33a83), 18 (pid26340, 73cb9ad7)}. Two builds of the same VB6 self-injecting loader discriminated by the JMP target E9 F7 07 00 00 (jmp 0x804 -> entry 0x804) and a classic EBP stack frame (55 8B EC push ebp/mov ebp,esp ; 83 EC 34). Intra-cluster ssdeep 94 and 99.1% position-wise byte identity. Every A-vs-B cross pair drops to ssdeep 52-58 and ~36.9% byte identity -> a hard cluster boundary. Both A members executed on win2008R2 controllers under the f-response-lm- process label.

evidence.discriminator: E9 F7 07 00 00 (jmp 0x804) + EBP frame (55 8B EC ; 83 EC 34)

findings.description: Cluster B = {19 (pid145896, e855864a), 20 (pid151132 femc, dd8ac01d), 21 (nfury pid328, a8f9a210)}. Same VB6 loader source recompiled with ESP-relative codegen: JMP target E9 60 08 00 00 (jmp 0x86D) and an ESP-relative frame (83 EC 30 sub esp,0x30 ; 8B 44 24 34). Intra-cluster ssdeep 91-97 (19<->21=97, 19<->20=96, 20<->21=91) and 98.7-99.8% byte identity. Cluster B spans two host OSes (win2008R2 controllers + win7-64 nfury WOW64), showing a single loader deployed enterprise-wide. The entry algorithm is byte-for-byte equivalent to Cluster A at the instruction-semantics level (same field reads, SHL by cl, 0x300/0x736 constants) -> same author, two compiler builds.

Injection / unpack technique (common to both variants): an in-memory unpack/self-injecting loader, NOT a remote download stub and NOT API-hash shellcode. The 8-byte little-endian header (0x08) is a length/offset prefix indicating code begins at offset 0x08, where an E9 rel32 JMP transfers to the real entry routine; the function immediately after the JMP (offset 0x0D) is an LZMA-family range decoder (signatures: shr esi,0xB, kTopValue 0x800, probability update shr 5, range-renorm threshold 0x1000000, prob tables via imul esi,esi,0xC00 / +0x1CD8). The entry routine receives a struct of pre-resolved kernel32 pointers ([+0x08]=VirtualAlloc, [+0x0C]=VirtualFree), computes a buffer size from header byte[hdr+4] (idiv 9, idiv 5, then ((0x300<<cl)+0x736)<<4), VirtualAlloc(NULL,size,MEM_COMMIT 0x1000,PAGE_READWRITE 0x04), runs the decoder at 0x0D to inflate an embedded LZMA-compressed blob, then VirtualFree(buf,0,MEM_RELEASE 0x8000) returning the decoded buffer to the caller. A PIC import resolver at file offset 0x10D8 (call $+5; pop ebx; sub ebx,<delta> self-locate) walks a plaintext import-name list (kernel32/user32 + OpenProcess/VirtualProtect/GetModuleHandleA/ExitProcess/CloseHandle/MessageBoxA/wsprintfA), supports ordinal imports (test eax,0x80000000 IMAGE_ORDINAL_FLAG), and writes resolved addresses into an IAT. The surrounding loader imports VirtualProtect (RWX flip) and OpenProcess (cross-process injection capability). Classic msvbvm60/VB6-packed self-injecting stub captured by Volatility malfind.

evidence.header_meaning: 8-byte LE prefix = 0x08 = offset of E9 JMP entry stub; code starts at 0x08
evidence.decoder: LZMA-family range decoder at offset 0x0D (kTopValue 0x800, prob shr 5, renorm 0x1000000, imul 0xC00 / +0x1CD8)
evidence.api_resolution: by plaintext name (GetModuleHandleA/LoadLibraryA + GetProcAddress), NOT API hashing; ordinal-import aware (IMAGE_ORDINAL_FLAG 0x80000000)

findings.description: Detection signature: YARA rule SRL2015_MemInject_VB_Family (srl2015_meminject.yar) detects the family across both variants and any future recompile. Anchors: 8-byte length header at offset 0 followed by E9 JMP loader stub ($hdr {08 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 E9} at 0), msvbvm (VB6 runtime), the OpenProcess/GetModuleHandleA/VirtualProtect injection API cluster, kernel32 import-resolver target, and a VB runtime-error string artifact OR the contiguous OpenProcess\x00GetModuleHandleA\x00VirtualProtect API table. Bounded filesize < 256KB for fast scanning of malfind dumps. Variant discriminators ($jmp_A 0x804 / $jmp_B 0x86D) retained for cluster attribution. Rule compiles clean (yara, exit 0).

IOC / C2 finding (negative, evidentiary): the 5 malfind 8KB dumps carry NO encoded/encrypted C2 or embedded configuration. Single-byte XOR brute force (keys 0x00-0xFF) combined with base64 detection across all 5 payloads, using a strict matcher for genuine network indicators (http(s)://, domains with common TLDs, IPv4+optional port, User-Agent, Mozilla/, cmd.exe, powershell, \pipe\, Global\ mutex prefix), produced 0 readable network indicators under any of the 256 keys; a looser regex produced only XOR-garbage false positives that resolved to no hostname/IP/URL. No base64 blob decoded to printable network strings. Payload-tail entropy (>=0x800) is ~3.97 bits/byte with 48.6% zero bytes -> far too low for an encrypted/packed config blob; the post-code region (>=0x900 in variant B) is captured Windows memory-manager metadata (repeating cookie c47e e7d5, addresses 00a00c00/00900b00, 0000ffff markers), i.e. VAD/heap structures snapshotted by the malfind dump. No embedded references to disk droppers (usboesrv.exe / a.exe / spinlock.exe / svchost.exe / femc / f-response / nfury) inside payload bytes; the link to host/process names is contextual (Volatility dump labels) only. The actionable IOCs are the 5 SHA256 hashes, the msvbvm60 VB6 injection signature, and the YARA rule -- the real C2 would live in the LZMA-decompressed second stage, which is not present in these dumped pages.
